purpose: Freeze referral reassignment coupling to open assessment assignment across local-file and PostgreSQL adapters, and retain the failing observation that exposed the PostgreSQL defect.
boundedContract: A supervisor-created referral assigned to assessor A records the supervisor as creator and assigning supervisor and assessor A as assignee.
An open assessment created by assessor A inherits assessor A's id and display name.

A supervisor reassignment to assessor B records the supplied handoff reason, removes assessor A's assignee access, preserves the supervisor's creator and assigning-supervisor responsibilities, and gives assessor B assignee access.
The open assessment changes to assessor B, increments exactly one version, and records one assessment_assigned audit event attributed to the supervisor.

PostgreSQL performs the referral, assessment, work-item, audit, and revision effects in one transaction; local-file mode provides the same successful domain result without claiming equivalent failure atomicity.

adapters.failure: Referral reassignment returned HTTP 500 before any coupled transaction effect committed.

diagnosis.source: PostgreSQL server log for the isolated PostgreSQL 16 cluster
diagnosis.error: could not determine data type of parameter $3
diagnosis.rollbackObserved: The referral, assessment, and audit rows remained at their pre-handoff versions after the failed transaction.

attempts.fix: Cast the nullable assessor-name SQL parameter to text at the jsonb_build_object call so PostgreSQL can type the prepared parameter without changing the stored JSON value.

claimBoundary: This evidence supports only the named successful handoff behavior on the recorded commit. It does not prove local failure atomicity, every reassignment race, signed/completed assessment behavior, or whole-application correctness.
